newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks seen starting softer, cautious tone.
newsitem.headline: French stocks seen starting softer, cautious tone.

text.p: The Paris bourse was expected to open lower, continuing Monday's decline, traders said.
Uncertainty over the euro would likely keep the market off-balance, following yesterday's request by France for a delay in signing a budget stability pact.
But volume was likely to be thin in cash stocks, with little sign on Monday of significant selling.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 33.05 points or 1.22 percent at 2,686.20. The CAC-40 futures contract on GLOBEX was down 17 at 2,651 from Monday's close.

The market appeared to be correcting the rise seen since the Socialists' French election win, an outcome which many had expected to lead to sharp losses in share prices, especially if there were a need for Communist support, one broker said.
"I'm surprised (at the market's rise), it looks like we are seeing the correction," he said.
* Renault will likely feature, with its shareholders' meeting today. The car maker declined comment on Belgian daily Le Soir's report that the closure of the Vilvoorde factory will be delayed.
* Communications stocks may also hold market attention.
* The Socialist government is considering lowering the maximum equity stake in broadcasters to 25 percent from 49, which is expected to hit holding companies, brokers said.
The new administrator is viewed as hostile to private broadcaster TF1, whose licence is held by building company Bouygues.
